newsitem.title: USA: US bank regulator praises "capital allocation" use.
newsitem.headline: US bank regulator praises "capital allocation" use.

text.p: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig Tuesday praised the growing use of a new method of risk management used by banks known as "capital allocation."

"I welcome the development," Ludwig said in a statement accompanying the release of an OCC study on capital allocation, a process by which economic capital is assigned to transactions, products, customers or units to provide management with risk-adjusted profitability measures.
"I encourage banks to consider using innovative tools such as capital allocation," Ludwig said.

Using capital allocation, a bank may realize that a particular highly profitable activity is tying up substantially more capital than a less profitable activity because of the potential risks or volatility involved.
The OCC survey of 10 large banks found that capital allocation processes and objectives for such systems varied widely.
Such systems "need to be adapted to the specific needs and requirements of each institution," Ludwig said, noting that even the most effective methods had some limitations.

Capital allocation is most useful for large, sophisticated companies whose senior management are removed from day-to-day pricing decisions and need information on risk-taking decisions facing the bank, OCC said.
The process creates a "framework for better informed decisions that result in improved bank performance and enhanced safety and soundness," OCC said.
Capital allocation is not related to calculating a bank's regulatory capital requirements, which all banks must meet, OCC noted.
